posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
So--a pretty simple question, and one that's probably been asked a few times when the game first came out, but not as much since Shattered Timelines has come out:

Who's your favorite character?  Who's the Hero that you find yourself picking more often than the others or that just suits your play style?

 

For me, It's Bunker.  I'm an unapologetic Iron Man fanboy, so Bunker fits that thematic niche for me.  I find that Bunker can alternate between pure DPS to tanking, all the while fueling either consistent damage (via Gatling Gun) or priming that OmniCannon for a big blast.

I'm also a huge fan of Iron/Dark Age comics, to the point where I wrote my own RPG to emulate Watchmen/The Dark Knight Returns and the like, which I Kickstarted last year.  I love the idea of the tortured hero facing down ethical challenges, which leads me straight towards Expatriette.  Plus, there's nothing more satisfying to me than pulling off a massive Unload, letting loose a whole arsenal's worth of bullets and eviscerating everything on the field.

But, when I'm in a bind and don't know who to pick?  I find myself gravitating more and more towards Fanatic.  She's just so versatile:  she can tank, she can deal damage, she can heal, she can destroy Ongoings and Environments...just an all-around great choice.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
I really enjoy playing Chrono Ranger, and played him a lot once Shattered Timelines came out. But I think the Adept has moved back to the top of the pile again - there's always something you can do on his turn, so you never have to sit there waiting for a useful card to turn up or whatever, because you can always stick a new song out or something. And getting other people to do stuff is cool, because you can normally squeeze at least a couple of extra actions (not necessarily yours) out of your turn. I like using the Harp to activate Superhuman Tonic, which I use to activate the Lyra (or the other way round), which activates Superhuman Tonic, which activates whichever instrument would be useful right now, which activates whichever song(s) would be useful right now…then I go back and finish off the Lyra and the Harp's actions.

Other than that, if I'm in a new situation and want a general all-rounder to do stuff, I'll quite often go with Wraith.

posts.cooked: Nightmist is definitely my favorite hero, there's a reason I have a booth banner on my wall of her. posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
I have three heroes that I would equally go to if I were to choose a heroes if not playing random. Absolute Zero, he is a wrecking machine! Can rack up tons of damage. Once he has burned away his last bit of HP, he can start allowing allowing other heroes use powers, thus giving them the chance to catch up with the damage he has done. He also may have the strongest Ongoing destruction in the game, which is awesome!

The next up is Tempest, the alien with high damage output. He is able to wipe out armies and armies of minions, while landing massive hits on the main villain. He moves through his deck swiftly, so he can easily get to what he needs. Not only does he have ongoing and environment destruction, but he can toss cards in play back ontop of the villain deck.

The invulnerable NightMist, she is able to heal to passively that she is nearly unkillable. Not having to waste a card play to recover that HP is great, it just comes with playing spells and discarding at the end. Plus her redirection makes it even harder to kill, as she can prevent herself from taking for much damage. She is a force to be reckoned with!

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Visionary.

I GM a lot, and Visionary gives me that sort of overarching control of the situation without being the star of the show.  Randomly pulling off things like one-shotting Omnitron with wrest the mind, or making AZ unkillable with a Twist the Ether, feeding cards to the right players at the right time, it's just fun.  I don't like Dark Visionary as well, mostly because every time I play her someone gets an horrible draw and I keep thinking I could have fixed that.

Argent Adept is my second favorite.  I dont like his dependence on cards in play to do anything, but he's amazing otherwise.  Other people have started getting into Adept too, so I rarely play him anymore.

When I have to be a damage dealer I go straight to Expat, although I've been trying Bunker more (after I complained about how terrible he was for so long) and I'm starting to like him, although in 18 games as Bunker I have yet to fire the Omni-cannon, I rarely get it and when I do I don't have cards or the set up to use it.

The only heroes I don't like playing are Ra and Nightmist.  I don't like pure nukers, I don't find them fun, and Nightmist I feel like I'm taking forever and doing all kinds of game mechanic and at the end of the match most times I feel like it didn't accomplish much at all.  I personally think of her as a busy and less stable version of Visionary, but I know others find her much better.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
NightMist, which is hilarious to me because I really disliked her at first, but, like Orphanleni, once I'd studied her a bit and grokked her, I found her to be incredibly powerful. I am envious of the NightMist banner ...

 

Playing NightMist requires a lot of challenging choices. Get more cards, or get out another way to heal? Will it be more important to heal in the future, do damage, or manipulate something? Once you have the amulet, you need to discard all the time, so you have to make lots of judgements about what's the most important to keep. When is it important to keep a card with '1' magic point that you think you _might_ need versus keeping a card with '4' magic points that you probably won't need?

posts.name: Chromium_Man
posts.cooked:
Like PlatinumWarlock, I am an unapologetic Iron Man. I assumed when I purchased the game that Bunker would be my favorite too but I have yet to have that breakthrough game with him where I really fall in love. 

Instead, favorite hero honors go to the other powered armor guy: Absolute Zero.  Without exaggeration I can say that he is the reason I got this game. I was debating Kickstarting IR/EE but wasn't sure. I love super heroes and board games but I've been skunked on a few games that are very well liked. It was a post on BGG complaining about how Absolute Zero was too difficult and counterintuitive that convinced me that I would like this game. I'm still no AZ expert but I'm getting close :)

Although she doesn't appeal to me thematically, I really like the complexity of Nightmist. I think I'll work on her next. Plus I just picked up Arkham Horror (featuring Faye's grandfather) and once I've played it, I think I'll find her theme more enjoyable.
